title: 4. Citizenship at the Commencement of the Constitution (Article 5)

blocks.content:
A person was considered an Indian citizen on 26 January 1950 if he or she:

• Was domiciled in India, and
• Was born in India, or
• Had either parent born in India, or
• Had been ordinarily resident in India for at least five years before commencement.

A person was considered an Indian citizen on 26 January 1950 if he or she:• Was domiciled in India, and• Was born in India, or• Had either parent born in India, or• Had been ordinarily resident in India for at least five years before commencement.

items: Domicile in India is a mandatory requirement under Article 5—it must be combined with at least one secondary condition.
The minimum period of ordinary residence required prior to commencement is exactly 5 years.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 5 governs citizenship strictly at the commencement of the Constitution on 26 January 1950.
Being domiciled in India is a compulsory baseline condition for citizenship under this Article.
In addition to domicile, a person must fulfill at least one of three secondary conditions: self-birth in India, parent's birth in India, or 5 years of ordinary residence prior to commencement.
